evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said 'Specifically would take about maybe 7 to 10 minutes. Then you can walk away with a quote you can depend on. Sounds good.' — no wait for affirmative yes, customer says 'Okay, yes' but rep had already moved on.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked: 'So other than the price, what are your biggest concerns and any questions you want answers to on this call?' — asked before any probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised two concerns: (1) efficiency/timing of move-out same day as key return, and (2) need for help with beds/reassembly as a single mom of three. Rep acknowledged with 'Got it. Yeah,' then immediately pivoted into a full Two Promises pitch about professional crew, furniture disassembly, damage coverage, and on-time guarantee — no 'tell me more about that' or deeper follow-up on either concern.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Rep acknowledged ('Got it. Yeah') but did not reflect back: 'So what I'm hearing is you're concerned about timing and efficiency, and you need help with furniture reassembly because you're moving solo with three kids — did I get that right?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gave typical range: 'typically two bedroom apartment takes three and a half to five and a half hours' and personalized to this move: 'in your case since you're coming from a third floor, I would estimate your move to take about two and a half to four and a half hours with two movers.' Anchor present and personalized.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee, overnight fee, fuel surcharge, elevator fees all explicitly disclosed: 'we don't have any extra charges Tianna we don't have credit card fees, no transfer transportation fees, no fuel surcharges and no several or elevator fees.' Minimum and increments stated: 'two and a half hour minimum... prorated in fifteen minute increments.' Full framing present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep asked 'Does that feel fair?' and customer responded immediately without rep filling silence: 'Yeah, so you said $119 an hour...' — silence held, real pause.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep stated: 'If we're late $50 comes off immediately and after the first hour is an extra $25 for every thirty minutes after that.' — discount terms stated in recognizable form.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep stated: 'No worries, damage coverage up to $2,000 included in the rate. And we pay it out in four to six days.' — coverage amount and inclusion in rate stated, but rep did not explicitly frame 'no deductible / no fine print' language.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent confirmation after delivering Two Promises. No loop-closing question present.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asked 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine final concerns check. Moved straight to sending email quote without this section.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asked 'would you like our help with your move or you still want decide?' — softened with an immediate out ('or you still want decide'), reducing the strength of the ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep stated: 'when you book your rate locks. So if already go up between now and your move day you still pay today's and there's again there's no deposit.'
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: No booking confirmed at all. Customer explicitly declined to book ('I'm still gonna call different people, I'm still comparing and pricing'), and rep accepted the objection without attempting to move forward, schedule, or even collect a tentative hold date/phone confirmation. Call ended with promise to send email; no crew notes, dates, window, or addresses confirmed for a booking.

top_strength: Rep executed a nearly flawless logistics discovery (Section 3) — gathered property type, floor, walking distance, room count, and special items with a systematic, efficient line of questioning that covered all seven items and set up a solid estimate.
coaching_note: Section 2 engagement must be deeper: when the customer raised two real pain points (efficiency + single-parent staffing), rep pivoted straight into Two Promises benefits instead of asking 'tell me more about that' — missing the chance to connect those promises directly to her stated needs, which likely cost the close.
booking_note: Customer explicitly stated she is 'still gonna call different people' and is 'comparing and pricing,' declining to commit despite receiving a quote.
